images.seen: A scruffy dog lying on a blanket on a stoep beside strelitzias, damp concrete, heavy grey sky over a lush garden. Tuesday.
lines: A grey day reads the same in any language: blanket, stoep, minimal ambition.
The concrete is still damp and the sky looks like it isn't finished.
Under a sky like this the whole garden runs at half-speed, dog included.

images.seen: A man at the end of his wet driveway, back to camera, umbrella in one hand and sunglasses in the other, under a broken grey sky with bright patches. Thursday.
lines: Umbrella in one hand, sunglasses in the other — he has met this sky before.
That sky refuses to commit, so he came prepared for both of its moods.
Bring a jacket. Or sunscreen. Or both.

images.seen: An estate street split down the middle — deep blue sky and sunlit lawns on one side, a dark advancing wall of cloud on the other. Monday.
lines: Half this street is in summer and the other half is about to be somewhere else.
That cloud line is moving in with the confidence of a Monday.
The blue half of the sky is on borrowed time and the lawns know it.
